title: The Accounting Equation
html:
The basic equation

Assets = Liabilities + Equity

This equation is one of the foundations of accounting. Every transaction must keep the equation balanced.

Assets

Assets are resources controlled by a business that are expected to provide future economic benefit.

Examples include cash, inventory, equipment, buildings and accounts receivable.

Liabilities

Liabilities are obligations the business owes to others.

Examples include accounts payable, loans payable and wages payable.

Equity

Equity represents the owners' residual interest in the assets after liabilities are deducted.

Example

A business has $50,000 of assets and $20,000 of liabilities.

Equity must equal:

$50,000 − $20,000 = $30,000

Remember

  • The accounting equation must always balance.
  • Assets are resources.
  • Liabilities are obligations.
  • Equity is the owners' residual interest.

quiz.prompt: A company has $80,000 of assets and $25,000 of liabilities. What is equity?
